sources.critical_scope: The indexed 1722 wording appears to refer to good DAYS for arts, not verified birth-day personalities. Do not force this into Yucatec Bolles natal rule.

semantic_distinctions: Chuen-as-artisan noun and Hun Chuen patron deity are linguistic/mythological statements, not empirical birth-day propensity.
Bolles compiled text explicitly says anyone born under each named day; this is an actual natal-ascription text class but composite of dependent witnesses.
Aztec Ozomatli day-born arts description in Thompson is separate Nahua tradition, not an independent modern Mayan individual effect.
Highland 1722 Ahilabal text may concern auspicious DAYS for arts; its 52-group math and source text are not a Yucatec birth-ascription duplicate.
Men may denote skilled maker or ritual specialist depending on language/era; never use generic maker lexical meaning to pool all maker signs as one frozen primary test.
Yucatec Chuen = Highland B'atz' linguistic crosswalk only; no universal count-date mapping.

existing_prior_art.policy: This audit upgrades ONLY historical semantic corroboration; does not change Gregorian GMT correlation selection or validate day-boundary, cohort, outcome score.
